neighbours.label: confirm / secure in the sense of making a right, grant or status firm
fire: In 1334 the town obtained from the king a confirmation of its charter.
The gift of land was later confirmed by his brother and heir.
They appointed a captain in order to secure their right to the pasture.
The treaty was signed to secure the borders of the young kingdom.
The bishop confirmed the monks in possession of the mill.
The council voted to confirm the grant made by the late earl.
He worked for years to secure a pension for the widows.
The new charter secured the merchants' freedom from tolls.
quiet: In 1334 the town obtained from the king a copy of its charter.
The gift of land was later disputed by his brother and heir.
They appointed a captain in order to defend the village from raids.
The treaty was signed to end the war of the young kingdom.
The bishop visited the monks in their house by the mill.
The council voted to review the grant made by the late earl.
He worked for years to write a history of the widows.
The new charter described the merchants' guild and its tolls.
